prior_evidence: readonly.py:571-586 _parse_statements returns list[exp.Expression | None] (None possible for empty statement) and wraps only sqlglot ParseError/TokenError as UnsafeSqlError('could not parse SQL: ...'). But the claim says ambiguous MySQL token boundaries also yield a message starting 'could not parse SQL'. _mysql_parse_sql (readonly.py:511-568) raises UnsafeSqlError directly with other messages ('MySQL backslash-escaped quotes are not allowed' 528, 'MySQL executable comments are not allowed' 541, 'Unterminated MySQL comment' 544, 'Nested MySQL comments are not allowed' 546, 'Ambiguous MySQL double-dash syntax is not allowed' 552, 'Ambiguous line-comment carriage return...' 562); these are not ParseError/TokenError so are not rewrapped. Rejections lines cover other issues, not this. Claim's message prefix is wrong for the ambiguity case. Callers (whole_row.py:101) only rely on UnsafeSqlError, so impact is low.
